refuters.argument:
After a clause-by-clause comparison of the printed CV def:polygon (reference/R/CV/d1_setup.tex 8-19) with the Lean primitives CV.IsPolygon / CV.Consecutive / CV.Remote / CV.RemoteToVertex and the bundle CV.PolygonData (statement file lines 47-159), I found no labelled tuple, no pair of indices, and no printed clause on which they disagree. I therefore cannot refute the row.

What I checked, primitive by primitive:

1. "tuple P in (R^2)^n with p_{i+1} != p_i for every i, indices cyclically modulo n" -> `IsPolygon P := ∀ i, edge P i ≠ 0` with `SM.edge P i = P (i+1) - P i` (SM/Polygon.lean:49) on `LabelledTuple n = ZMod n → Plane`; `isPolygon_iff` (line 49) gives exactly `∀ i, P (i+1) ≠ P i`. The 0-based ZMod labelling versus the printed 1..n labelling is a successor-preserving relabelling and changes nothing. Field `polygon` (line 137) carries the printed `n ≥ 3`.

2. "edges are the closed segments e_i = [p_i, p_{i+1}]" -> field `edge_segment` (141-142): `edgeSegment P i = segment ℝ (P i) (P (i+1))`; I confirmed Mathlib's `segment` is the closed segment (`#print segment`, `segment_eq_image'` : image of `Set.Icc 0 1`).

3. "edge directions d_i = p_{i+1} - p_i in R^2 \ {0}" -> fields `edge_direction` (144) and `direction_ne_zero` (146); the latter is literally IsPolygon.

4. "Two edges are consecutive if their index sets meet" -> `Consecutive i j := ∃ k, (k = i ∨ k = i+1) ∧ (k = j ∨ k = j+1)` (line 54) = the vertex-index sets {i,i+1} and {j,j+1} intersect. Kernel-checked (scratch copy of the reviewer-input definitions, `decide`) exhaustively for n = 3,4,5,6,7 against `(({i,i+1} : Finset (ZMod n)) ∩ {j,j+1}).Nonempty`. Same edge is consecutive to itself under both readings (index sets coincide), so `Remote i i` false is not a disagreement.

5. "and remote otherwise" -> `Remote i j := ¬ Consecutive i j` (line 57). Field `remote` records ↔ SM.remote; kernel-checked at n=5 (SM.adjacent) as a sanity check.

6. "An edge is remote to a vertex p_M when it is remote to both edges incident to M" -> `RemoteToVertex M j := Remote j (M-1) ∧ Remote j M` (line 62). Under e_i = [p_i,p_{i+1}] the edges containing p_M are e_{M-1} and e_M, so this is exactly the printed (stronger) reading. Kernel-checked for n = 3..7: `RemoteToVertex M j ↔ j ∉ {M-2, M-1, M, M+1}`; the printed non-example (n=4, vertex 0, edge e_2 avoids p_0 but shares p_3 with e_3) is correctly NOT remote-to-vertex; at n=5, vertex 0, exactly e_2 qualifies; `RemoteToVertex M j → ¬ SM.incident M j` (n=6) holds, matching "the stronger of the two possible readings" (field `remote_to_vertex_stronger`, line 155, is a consequence of the printed text, not added content).

7. "We write det(u,v) = u_1 v_2 - u_2 v_1" -> field `det_formula` (157); `SM.det u v = u.1 * v.2 - u.2 * v.1` (SM/Polygon.lean:16).

8. "indices read cyclically modulo n throughout" -> field `cyclic` (139), `P (i + n) = P i`, which is trivially true in ZMod n (cast of n is 0) but faithfully records that cyclicity lives in the index type.

Every printed sentence has a field and every field traces to a printed sentence; no field narrows the domain to SM's quotient or to any locus (decision F2 respected: everything is on labelled tuples, "a polygon is a tuple").

Observations that are NOT discrepancies but worth recording: (a) `IsPolygon` itself has no `n ≥ 3` hypothesis — the printed "Let n ≥ 3" is carried only as `_hn : 3 ≤ n` in the `polygon` field, so e.g. the 2-tuple ((0,0),(1,0)) satisfies `IsPolygon` (kernel-checked) although the printed text defines no polygon on 2 vertices. This is a domain broadening (same convention the accepted SM lane uses: "Helpers on labelled tuples are also defined at smaller sizes"), not a narrowing, and downstream consumers must carry `3 ≤ n` themselves. (b) `cyclic` is a tautology in ZMod n. Neither gives a concrete tuple or index pair on which the printed notion and the Lean notion give different answers within the printed domain n ≥ 3.
